summary:
LIFE: YOUR CHOICE is an interactive, story-driven educational game that lets players experience life as a NASA systems engineer while exploring the relationship between professional success and personal happiness.

Created for the Space Mission Design Game challenge, our project introduces players to engineering decision-making through scenarios inspired by NASA's Systems Engineering Handbook. Players make choices about component testing and mission-related engineering tasks, receive feedback through an engineering scoring system, and learn how decisions can affect mission outcomes.

What makes our game unique is its integration of personal life decisions. Alongside engineering challenges, players navigate friendships, family relationships, and career opportunities. These choices influence the story and lead to different endings.

By connecting engineering decisions with real-life trade-offs, our game encourages players to think critically, learn from their choices, and recognize that professional achievement alone does not define a fulfilling life.
details:
LIFE: YOUR CHOICE

Design a Space Mission. Shape Your Life.

Project Overview

LIFE: YOUR CHOICE is an interactive educational game designed to introduce players to NASA systems engineering while encouraging reflection on the personal decisions that shape their lives.

Players begin their journey as newly hired NASA engineers. Throughout the game, they encounter engineering challenges, make technical decisions, earn or lose points based on their answers, and experience events involving their professional and personal lives.

Our goal is to make systems engineering more accessible and engaging while presenting an additional question: What does success mean beyond professional achievement?

Addressing the NASA Space Apps Challenge

Our project was developed in response to the Space Mission Design Game challenge, which emphasizes engineering decision-making, resource constraints, trade-offs, and learning from the consequences of design choices.

Our current approach focuses on the decision-making and educational feedback aspects of space mission engineering.

Players encounter technical scenarios related to spacecraft component testing and mission development. They must evaluate available choices and select appropriate engineering approaches.

The game uses a scoring system to provide feedback on technical decisions, helping players recognize the importance of engineering requirements, testing, safety, and risk management.

The engineering content is informed by principles presented in the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook.

How the Game Works

1. Character Creation

Players begin by choosing their character's name and gender, allowing them to participate in the story as their own NASA engineer.

2. Engineering Challenges

Players encounter engineering-related scenarios, including decisions about component testing and verification. They select possible approaches based on the situation presented.

3. Engineering Feedback

Technical decisions affect the player's engineering score. This feedback encourages players to evaluate their choices and learn from the outcomes.

4. Personal Life Events

Alongside engineering tasks, players encounter events involving friendships, family, and career decisions.

For example, a player may need to decide whether to dedicate additional time to work or spend time with a friend.

5. Different Endings

The choices players make influence the direction of the story and its ending.

A player may achieve professional success while neglecting important relationships. Other decisions can lead to different personal outcomes, encouraging players to explore multiple perspectives.

Our Unique Approach: Engineering and Life

Traditional engineering education primarily focuses on technical knowledge and professional performance.

Our game expands this perspective by connecting technical decision-making with personal life choices.

In space mission design, engineers must consider mission requirements, limited resources, competing constraints, and the consequences of their decisions.

We recognized that everyday life also involves trade-offs. Time spent pursuing one goal may reduce the time available for other meaningful activities.

By incorporating both types of decisions, LIFE: YOUR CHOICE provides an experience that connects engineering thinking with human values.

We also believe that personal well-being and meaningful relationships can support motivation, resilience, and long-term professional growth.

Our goal is not to suggest that one lifestyle is better than another. Instead, we want players to discover what matters to them and understand that happiness cannot be measured by professional achievement alone.

Educational Value and Potential Impact

LIFE: YOUR CHOICE aims to:

  • Introduce students and aspiring engineers to NASA systems engineering concepts through interactive decisions.
  • Make technical learning more approachable through storytelling, feedback, and game-based experiences.
  • Encourage players to consider how decisions affect both professional and personal outcomes.
  • Inspire reflection on personal values, well-being, and the meaning of success.
  • Demonstrate how engineering concepts can connect with challenges beyond the technical workplace.

Development Tools and Technologies

We developed LIFE: YOUR CHOICE as a browser-based, interactive career simulation game using Vue 3, TypeScript, and Vite.

Vue.js powers the visual novel-style interface, while Vue Router manages navigation, Pinia handles game state, and Vue I18n provides full Japanese and English language support.

At the core of the game, we built a custom, data-driven story engine in TypeScript. It processes dialogue, branching decisions, multiple-choice selections, conditional logic, randomized outcomes, and changes to the player's career and personal life.

Our simulation introduces engineering trade-offs through six resources: budget, time, mass, power, data, and communications. Players must balance technical constraints, evaluate risks, and make decisions that affect their performance, career progression, and work–life balance. The game also features personal storylines that respond to the player's choices and circumstances.

For development and quality assurance, we used Vitest and Vue Test Utils to test game mechanics, story branches, scoring, and user interface behavior. GitHub supports version control and collaboration, while Netlify hosts and deploys the web application.

We also incorporated AI-assisted development tools into our workflow. Claude Code supported implementation, debugging, and testing, while ChatGPT assisted with story development, technical planning, and the generation of original character illustrations and background artwork.

The application runs entirely in the browser, making it accessible without requiring installation or a dedicated backend server.

Conclusion

LIFE: YOUR CHOICE brings together two kinds of learning: understanding how engineers make decisions in space missions and exploring how personal choices shape a fulfilling life.

Space missions have objectives and measurable requirements. Personal happiness, however, does not have one universal definition.

Through this game, we hope players will gain a greater appreciation of systems engineering and feel encouraged to make thoughtful choices about their own futures.

Design a Space Mission. Shape Your Life.
